sections.heading: Coming to the God I can truly know, but never fully contain
sections.text:
God, you are far greater than I can understand, and yet you let me know you truly. You have revealed yourself, even though there is still so much about you that is beyond me.

My needs, my troubles, and my longing for what is good pull me toward you. You have never invited anyone to seek you for nothing. So I come to you with my difficulties, my needs, and my distress. Hear me, and draw me near.
theological_themes: God is both revealed and incomprehensible; he can be truly known without being exhaustively understood.
God hears prayer and does not call his people to seek him in vain.
Need and distress rightly drive the believer toward God rather than away from him.

scripture_references.connection: God explicitly says he has not called his people to seek him in emptiness or chaos. This grounds the prayer’s confidence that coming to God in need is not pointless.
The psalm addresses God as the one who hears prayer, which supports the opening movement of approaching him with real wants and distress.
Paul worships God as beyond searching out, while still speaking truly about his wisdom and ways. This fits the prayer’s tension: God is known, yet beyond complete human knowledge.

sections.heading: Asking you to make prayer the shape of my life
sections.text:
Please fill my life with more of yourself. Give me the help of your Spirit, a heart that wants to pray, and a settled habit of turning toward you.

Bring me into warm fellowship with you, not only in set times of prayer, but in the ordinary business of the day. Let my thoughts and desires keep rising to you while I work, rest, speak, plan, and deal with people.

Make prayer a steady refuge for me: quieting my sorrows, keeping my successes from making me proud, and shaping the way I treat others.
theological_themes: Prayer is not only an occasional act but a posture of dependence on God throughout ordinary life.
The Holy Spirit enables prayer and communion with God.
Fellowship with God comforts sorrow, humbles success, and prepares the believer to love others rightly.

scripture_references.connection: Paul teaches that the Spirit helps believers in weakness and intercedes according to God’s will. This supports the request for a prayerful life empowered by God, not merely produced by human effort.
Believers have access to the Father through Christ and in the Spirit. This gives biblical grounding for asking to be brought into real fellowship with God.
Paul calls believers to do all things in the name of the Lord Jesus, with thanksgiving. That supports the desire for ordinary concerns, relationships, and duties to be lived before God.

sections.heading: Thanking you that I was made to know, reflect, and enjoy you
sections.text: Thank you that you made me able to know you, the Maker of everything. Thank you that you are making me able to become like you in holiness and love. Thank you that you are not only my duty, but my happiness—that the deepest joy I can have is found in you.
theological_themes: Human beings are made for communion with God.
Knowing God is life-giving, not merely informational.
God’s people are being changed to reflect his character and find their joy in him.

scripture_references.connection: Jesus defines eternal life as knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he has sent. This grounds the prayer’s gratitude that knowing God is central to human life and blessedness.
Paul describes believers being transformed into the image of the Lord. This supports the request and gratitude that the believer can increasingly resemble God’s excellency.
David speaks of fullness of joy in God’s presence. This gives biblical support for the claim that God himself is the source of true happiness.

sections.heading: Walking the hard road with Christ representing me
sections.text:
God, stay with me through every part of this hard and testing journey. I still need the same guidance, protection, and comfort that I needed when I first began with you.

Let my faith become clearer to my own conscience and more visible to the people around me. While Jesus represents me before you in heaven, help me represent him faithfully here on earth. While he speaks for me, let my life speak praise for him.
theological_themes: The Christian life is a pilgrimage that requires God’s ongoing counsel, defense, and comfort.
Christ intercedes for his people before the Father.
The believer’s life on earth should reflect and praise the Christ who represents them in heaven.

scripture_references.connection: Hebrews teaches that Jesus is able to save completely because he always lives to intercede for those who draw near to God through him. This directly supports the prayer’s confidence that Christ represents the believer before God.

John describes Jesus Christ the righteous as the believer’s advocate with the Father. This clarifies the meaning of Christ pleading the believer’s cause without implying that the Father is unwilling to receive them.
Jesus calls his disciples to let their light be seen so that others glorify the Father. This supports the request that faith become visible to others in a way that displays God’s praise.

sections.heading: Remembering how you have carried me, and praising you again
sections.text:
Keep dealing with me in the gentle kindness you have already shown me. Whether I am awake or asleep, let your presence go with me and your blessing rest on me.

You have led me this far, and I have found that your promises are true. When I was weighed down with sorrow, you helped me. When I was afraid, you rescued me. When I felt close to despair, you lifted me up.

I belong to you, and I owe you my praise. So I praise you, my God.
theological_themes: God’s presence and blessing sustain the believer through all of life.
Past deliverance strengthens present trust in God’s promises.
Praise is the fitting response of one who has been helped, rescued, and upheld by God.

scripture_references.connection: This psalm portrays the Lord as the keeper of his people, watching over their going out and coming in. It supports the prayer’s request for God’s care whether waking or sleeping.
David testifies that the Lord answered him, delivered him from fears, and saved the poor man who cried to him. This closely matches the remembrance of God’s help in sorrow, fear, and despair.
Israel’s history is summarized with the statement that none of God’s good promises failed. This supports the believer’s testimony that God has led them and proved his promises true.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The phrase in the original, “While Jesus is representing me in heaven,” assumes Christ’s present heavenly intercession. This is a mainstream biblical doctrine, but it needed to be worded carefully so it did not sound as if the Father is reluctant to love or receive the believer.
The original speaks of being made capable of “resembling” God. I rendered this as being made like God in holiness and love, avoiding any implication that humans become divine in essence.
significant_interpretive_choices: I interpreted “possess me with thyself” as a request for God to fill and govern the believer’s life by his presence and Spirit, rather than as mystical absorption into God.

I rendered “sanctify my successes” as asking God to keep success from producing pride and to make it serve holiness. This preserves the Puritan concern that prosperity can be spiritually dangerous unless received before God.
I understood “Thy vows are ever upon me” as the believer’s continuing obligation and belonging to God, not as a reference to a specific formal vow ceremony.
